name: fmt_choice_resolves_to_label
note: displayValue() resolves a choice CODE to its author-defined LABEL from config.options — the reason TemplateSources must thread `config` through. A naive renderer emits 'ncr'.

name: fmt_multi_select_joins
note: The join is '; ' — the same separator an export cell uses, which is the point of reusing displayValue().

name: fmt_yes_no_truthy_string
note: boolLabel()'s truthy set is a CLOSED literal list: true, int 1, and the strings '1','true','yes','on'.

name: fmt_yes_no_capital_yes_is_no
note: The trap this vector exists to pin: the truthy list is CASE-SENSITIVE, so 'Yes' is falsy. A TS mirror written from the type rather than from the list WILL diverge here.

name: fmt_integer_stored_as_string
note: A respondent's numeric answer persists as the SUBMITTED STRING (StructuralAnswerNormalizer), not as an int.

name: fmt_decimal_preserves_trailing_zero
note: Because the answer is the submitted string, '3.50' keeps its trailing zero. Contrast fmt_calculated_native_float: the SAME field type can hold two runtime types, so a vector must state which it pins. Coercion::toStr() is barred here (Doc #26 §3.2) precisely because its non-integral float parity is unpinned.

name: fmt_calculated_native_float
note: A `calculated` answer is stored as the evaluator's NATIVE float, unlike a respondent-typed decimal. `calculated` is pipeable in H6a and excluded from OCR — one of the two deliberate divergences from OcrFieldEligibility.

name: fmt_unanswered_renders_empty
note: Doc #26 §3.4 — an unanswered source renders as the EMPTY STRING, never the raw ${key} token and never a placeholder glyph. Publish refuses an unresolvable REFERENCE; render tolerates an unanswered VALUE.

name: fmt_option_label_resolves_locale
note: Increment H6b, amendment A8. Before it, displayValue() had no $locale at all and read config.options[].label raw — so a Filipino respondent got an English choice label dropped into the middle of a Filipino sentence, and the tenant's inbox disagreed with the respondent's own screen about the same answer. §4's order (resolve the locale, THEN render) now holds for the value as well as the sentence around it.

name: fmt_option_label_falls_back_to_base
note: Parity across locales is NOT required (§4) — an option with no variant for the active locale renders its base label, it is not an error and not a blank.

name: fmt_option_label_blank_variant_falls_back
note: The variant lookup mirrors resolveText(): a missing, non-string OR BLANK variant is no variant at all. A `??`-only mirror renders the blank. Note this is a DIFFERENT fallback from the base label's, which guards null only — see fmt_option_empty_label_wins.

name: fmt_option_label_ignored_without_a_locale
note: No locale means the base label, byte-identical to the pre-H6b behaviour — which is what keeps every existing caller that passes none unchanged.

name: fmt_bool_true_renders_one
note: Amendment A7. PHP casts a native bool to '1'/''; String(true) is 'true'. Reachable: the expression evaluator passes bools straight through, so a `calculated` field holding a comparison stores one, and `hidden` is server-constrained untrusted input.

name: fmt_bool_false_renders_empty
note: The nastier half: `false` is NOT caught by the empty guard (it is not null/''/[]), so it falls through to the cast and renders ''. A mirror using falsiness gets the right answer here for the wrong reason, then gets fmt_calculated_zero_renders_zero wrong.

name: fmt_calculated_non_integral_float
note: The value 0.1 + 0.2 actually produces. The bare casts disagree — PHP '0.3' (precision=14) vs JS '0.30000000000000004' — so A7 pins a fixed-notation rule both engines reproduce. H6a's only float vector was 3.5, exactly representable in binary, which concealed all of this.

name: fmt_calculated_repeating_float
note: 1/3. Ten decimals, trailing zeros trimmed — not PHP's precision=14 and not JS's shortest-round-trip 17.

name: fmt_calculated_large_float
note: Never E-notation: the bare PHP cast gives '1.0E+15'. The rule's integral branch is guarded at |v| < 1e21, which is exactly where JS toFixed falls back to exponential — the documented edge of the mirror, and why no vector may pin a value at or beyond it.

name: fmt_calculated_small_float
note: The other E-notation edge: the bare PHP cast gives '1.0E-5'.

name: fmt_calculated_zero_renders_zero
note: The empty guard is STRICT (=== null / === '' / === []), not falsy and not Coercion.isEmpty(). `if (!answer) return ''` would blank a running total of zero — the archetypal piping target.

name: fmt_cascading_select_resolves_labels
note: cascading_select is NOT in FieldType::hasOptions() — displayValue() adds it with an explicit `||`. A mirror reproducing only hasOptions() renders 'ncr; manila'. It is pipeable and had no vector before H6b.

name: fmt_likert_scale_numeric_value_resolves_label
note: Two traps at once: likert_scale is the fourth hasOptions() member, and the label map is keyed by the STRINGIFIED option value, so an integer answer finds an integer-valued option. A Map keyed by the raw value misses.

name: fmt_option_empty_label_wins
note: The BASE label falls back to the value on NULL ONLY, so an author's explicit empty label wins and renders empty. A mirror written as `label || value` renders 'na'. Contrast fmt_option_label_blank_variant_falls_back — the two levels have deliberately different fallbacks.

name: fmt_yes_no_unanswered_is_blank_not_no
note: Branch ORDER: the empty guard precedes the yes_no branch, so an unanswered yes/no is '' and not 'No'. A mirror that dispatches on type first is wrong on every unanswered yes/no field in the product.

name: fmt_yes_no_int_one_is_yes
note: The `=== 1` arm of the closed truthy set — the one member no other vector reaches. NOTE a 1.0 vector must NEVER be added: PHP's 1.0 === 1 is false while JSON 1 and 1.0 are the same JS number, an unfixable divergence recorded in display-value.ts.

name: fmt_multi_select_keeps_order_duplicates_and_unknowns
note: array_map + implode: NO sort, NO dedupe, NO filtering, and an unresolved element falls through to its own raw value. A mirror reaching for a Set, a sort, or `.filter(v => labels.has(v))` diverges.

name: fmt_object_answer_joins_values
note: json_decode($json, true) turns a JSON OBJECT into a PHP array, so is_array() is true and implode walks its VALUES. Array.isArray({}) is false, so a TS mirror falls to the scalar branch and emits the JSON text instead. Reachable because `hidden` is untrusted input.

name: fmt_unknown_key_renders_empty
note: A key ABSENT from `sources` appends nothing and never throws. Distinct from fmt_unanswered_renders_empty, which pins a KNOWN key with no answer. In TypeScript `sources[key]` is possibly-undefined, so the naive transcription throws right here.

name: fmt_hole_named_constructor_renders_empty
note: `constructor` is a GRAMMATICAL hole key ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*). Trivially '[]' in PHP; in TypeScript a bare `sources[key]` on an object literal returns Object.prototype.constructor — truthy, so the unknown-key guard does not fire and the hole renders its answer instead of nothing. The ANSWER is what makes this vector bite: without it the empty guard short-circuits first and the vector passes vacuously on both a correct and a prototype-unsafe mirror (found by mutation during H6b — the first version of this vector was green for the wrong reason).

name: fmt_escape_and_two_holes
note: Render composed with the grammar: `$${` yields the literal `${`, then two holes fill in order with literals interleaved. The escapes corpus pins the PARSER; nothing pinned escape-through-render.

name: fmt_geopoint_lat_first_with_accuracy
note: Three traps: the geo branch precedes the array join (which would otherwise stringify the envelope's keys), display is lat-FIRST while storage is lon-first, and coord() trims a fixed-7-decimal format. Unreachable through a published hole (geo is PipingEligibility::Excluded) — pinned so the SHARED formatter stays a complete twin, since an incomplete one fails invisibly the moment anything else reuses it.

name: fmt_geotrace_singular_point
note: The em dash is U+2014, the Line/Area noun split is by type, and the noun is singular at exactly one point.

name: fmt_media_names_the_files
note: Increment M74, the headline. Before it, an object-valued media answer reached displayValue()'s generic is_array join, which applies scalar() PER ELEMENT and json_encodes each envelope — so this rendered two escaped JSON blobs on the inbox, the export, the PDF and, through SubmissionRowProjector::answerValues(), into Google Sheets and Airtable. Names rather than a count because FieldInput.vue already decided that for the same answer on the encode screen: '2 files' gives an editor nothing to check against the paper form.

name: fmt_media_falls_back_to_mime_then_a_label
note: Both lower rungs, and neither is an edge case: `name` is OPTIONAL in the stored envelope (canonicalizeMediaRef copies it only when present and a string), so a camera capture routinely arrives with a mime and no filename. The `id` is deliberately NOT a rung — it is the right thing to show beside a control about to replace the file and the wrong thing to write into a record a human reads.

name: fmt_media_empty_list_is_blank
note: Branch ORDER, the media half: the empty guard precedes the media arm, so an unanswered upload is '' and never 'Attached file' or '0 files'. Same shape as fmt_yes_no_unanswered_is_blank_not_no, and the bracket device is borrowed from it so a blank is visible in the expectation.

name: fmt_matrix_keeps_row_identity
note: Increment M74. A matrix stores {row:{col:cell}}, and the generic join implodes an associative array's VALUES — so before this the row keys vanished entirely and the cells rendered as {"c1":"v1","c2":"v2"}; {"c1":"v3"}: machine noise AND missing the only thing that made the cells interpretable. Row and column VALUES, not labels; resolving those needs the field config threaded in and is its own row.

name: fmt_likert_matrix_keeps_row_identity
note: ⛔ THE VECTOR THAT CARRIES THIS INCREMENT, and the case the row that filed the defect did not contain. A likert_matrix stores {row:score} with SCALAR leaves, so the generic join emitted no JSON at all — just '4; 5; 3', every row label silently dropped and indistinguishable from a legitimate multi-select. That is not noise a reader discards; it is plausible WRONG DATA, and it was being written into third-party systems of record. A gate asserting 'the output contains no JSON' is GREEN against it, which is why this pins the whole string.

name: fmt_likert_matrix_integer_like_rows_sort_as_strings
note: Why the keys are SORTED at all, and it is the ordinary case rather than an exotic one: a grid whose rows are 1,2,3 is what a Likert grid looks like. PHP's json_decode keeps insertion order and turns "10" into the INT key 10; JavaScript's Object.keys hoists integer-like keys to the FRONT in numeric order. Unsorted twins therefore disagree on the most likely real input, and both would look right in isolation.

name: fmt_grid_keys_sort_by_code_point_not_utf16
note: ⛔ THE DISCRIMINATOR, AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED. PHP's sort(SORT_STRING) compares UTF-8 BYTES, which is CODE POINT order. JavaScript's default comparator compares UTF-16 CODE UNITS, where an astral character is a surrogate pair at U+D800-DBFF and so sorts BEFORE every BMP character from U+E000 up. ⚠️ A probe over ASCII, Tagalog diacritics and one emoji AGREED on both engines and concealed the whole question; this pairing of a fullwidth ＃ (U+FF03) with an emoji is what exposed it. display-value.ts therefore sorts by code point rather than with a bare .sort(), and a mutation replacing that comparator reddens this vector on the TypeScript side while PHP stays green — the asymmetry is the evidence.

name: fmt_likert_matrix_native_leaf_uses_the_pinned_rule
note: Amendment A7 reasserted at a NEW leaf. The grid arms route every cell through scalarString(scalar(v)) — the same primitive the list join uses — rather than a bare cast, so a native bool is '1' and not 'true' and a float takes the fixed-notation rule. ⚠️ THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS VECTOR USED true AND 0.1 AND A MUTATION PROVED IT VACUOUS: PHP casts both identically to the pinned rule ((string) true is 1, (string) 0.1 is 0.1), so replacing scalarString() with a bare cast SURVIVED. These three values are chosen because the casts DISAGREE — (string) 1/3 is 0.33333333333333 at precision=14, and (string) 1e-5 is 1.0E-5 — which is H6a-3.5 exactly, caught this time by the control rather than by the next increment.

name: fmt_matrix_malformed_renders_blank
note: Fail CLOSED, on formatGeo()'s precedent — a matrix answer that is a list is not a grid, and letting it fall through to the generic join is precisely the defect these arms exist to close. `hidden` is untrusted input and a stale offline client can post a shape the current schema does not describe, so this is reachable rather than defensive.
